records.description: The selected studies support ion- and sequence-dependent RNA conformation and reaction activity in prepared hammerhead complexes. Penedo loop perturbations shift global-FRET titrations and reduce a separate synthetic-RNA cleavage response. Boots finds similar global stem-proximity responses for four divalent ions despite markedly differing apparent reaction rates. Thus a global-folding proxy is insufficient to identify catalytic competence or a unique chemical mechanism; local structure, reactive population and chemistry remain distinct explanations.

records.name: Prepared HeLa intracellular reporter context
openObligations: The selected living-cell readout is the cytosolic-region optical ratio in prepared HeLa cultures. It is not a whole-cell extract, universal organelle redox value or measured free-cofactor potential.
DTT-induced reversal in the strong-challenge comparison is imposed externally. It demonstrates reversible reporter response, not spontaneous restoration by a cellular feedback circuit.

Short-lived responses at smaller challenges are consistent with reduction/recovery in the supplied cell culture. Peroxide removal, antioxidant turnover and reporter equilibration can all contribute; no unique endogenous recovery mechanism or feedback gain is identified.
The experiment does not directly measure GSH-regeneration flux, glutathione-reductase activity, NADPH turnover, electron transport, ATP generation or closed metabolic cycles.

No numerical dose, redox potential, compartmental concentration or recovery constant is newly admitted. Figure 2 has source-reported replicate/dispersion summaries, but raw single-cell trajectories, fit covariance and complete imaging artifacts were not independently audited.

records.name: Resolution-limited HEWL conformational comparison
openObligations: The selected experiment is a crystalline complex of harmless hen egg-white lysozyme and murine D1.3 Fab. It is not intact IgG avidity, an in-vivo immune response, a pathogen case, a clinical diagnostic validation or an affinity-engineering study.

Diffraction intensities and an electron-density/refinement model constrain geometry at 2.8 angstrom resolution; contacts, hydrogen bonds and accessible-area burial are assignments/calculations from that model, not directly measured interaction energies or a kinetic binding pathway.

The source gives R=0.28 over20-2.8 angstrom and an approximate coordinate error0.6 angstrom. Individual close-distance/strong-hydrogen-bond language is not promoted to exact bond lengths, energies, proton positions or independent energetic decomposition.

The unliganded D1.3 Fab structure had not been determined. Comparison with other antibodies does not supply a same-antibody before/after control, prove no loop adjustment or distinguish induced fit from conformational selection or lock-and-key binding.

The lysozyme comparison uses existing native crystal structures from other work. A small difference within error is not exact conformational identity in solution or evidence excluding all dynamic changes.
No solvent molecules were located in the refined model. A tentative density peak discussed as possible water is not a resolved hydration shell, water residence time or ionic distribution.

The printed affinity constant is attributed to Reference 25, an earlier/in-press source not independently read. Avian cross-reactivity discussion has limited assay information. No new binding constant, specificity panel, detection limit, mutational effect or quantitative discrimination claim is admitted.

The sequence assigned to Fab uses cDNA supplied through personal communication/Reference 13. Exact new sequencing, raw diffraction, original coordinates, refinement/covariance, salt effects and a kinetic mechanism are not reconstructed.

limitations: The new crystal is the double mutant Y16S/D40N with an intermediate analogue, not the catalytically assayed Y16S single mutant with reacting 5(10)-EST. D40N is introduced to mimic the protonated general-base state ; transferring structural interpretation to catalysis is conditional.

The proposed approximately 200-fold Tyr16 contribution relative to aqueous hydrogen bonding is explicitly crude and assumes cavity-water energetics resemble the solution reference and no propagating structural effects. It is not an admitted exact universal catalytic energy.
